translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 5.10.2016 (radio)
96 per cent of Finns trust the police. MPs do not accept violence by extremist groups. There are many Finnish medical students in Latvia. Finns want public art in their living environment.
## People trust the police
![Trust in the police.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9210910)
Open image viewer
Photo: Yle Uutisgrafiikka
Finns firmly trust the police. 96 per cent of Finns say that the police are fairly reliable or very reliable.
Finns' trust in the police has only grown since 2014, although the police have recently also been criticised.
In Finns' view, the police are the most important authority in preventing crime and improving security.
Only the fire and rescue service comes before the police in trust. 99 per cent of Finns trust it.
The information comes from a new survey made by the Police University College. About 1,000 people answered the survey.
## Extremist groups and violence
![The Resistance Movement at Narinkkatori in Helsinki.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-8758507)
Open image viewer
The neo-Nazi Finnish Resistance Movement is one of the extremist groups whose banning has been discussed. Photo: Yle
Finnish extremist groups and violence have been discussed in Parliament.
The parties agree that violence by extremist groups cannot be accepted. The parties, however, disagreed about banning extremist groups.

For example, the National Coalition Party was of the view that the matter must be investigated. The Finns Party, on the other hand, said that extremist groups should not be shut down, but violence must be dealt with using current legislation.
## Becoming a doctor in Latvia
![Susanna Luontola and Eva Tuuppa.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9203629)
Open image viewer
Susanna Luontola and Eva Tuuppa are studying to become doctors in Latvia. Photo: Eduards Lakis
There are many young Finns in Latvia who are studying there to become doctors.
About 150 Finns study medicine at the universities of Riga, the capital of Latvia. About 10 of them study to become dentists and the rest to become doctors.

Many Finns apply to study in Latvia, because there it may be easier to get a study place than in Finland. In Latvia you do not need to take entrance exams, but students are chosen on the basis of their papers.
Studying to become a doctor takes 6 years in Latvia. Tuition fees can be as much as 10,000 euros a year.
The Latvian medical degree is also valid in Finland, because both countries are EU countries.
## Art in the city
![Graffiti painting under the Toivonimi bridge in Oulu.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9210659)
Open image viewer
Finns want to see street art such as graffiti. Photo: Risto Degerman / Yle
Finns want there to be works of art in their living environment. Especially in the capital area and in Oulu, people want to see public art in their everyday environment.

In a survey by the Finnish Artists' Association, 80 per cent of Finns say that there must be art in hospitals and care homes. Almost as many also want to see street art, such as wall paintings and graffiti.
People think that art improves the pleasantness and safety of the environment.
